# Code of conduct

KingresDB is built by people who disagree about technical questions and still have to work together. This code of conduct says how we do that. It applies to every space of the project: the repository, issues, pull requests, discussions, the wiki and any other place where someone speaks for or about the project.

## What we expect

- Be respectful. Argue about the work, not about the person.
- Be precise and honest. Say what you verified and what you did not. Report a failure as a failure.
- Accept review. Give reviews that name the problem and, where you can, a way to fix it. Take reviews of your own work as help.
- Assume good faith until a pattern shows otherwise, and ask before you conclude.
- Respect other people's time and effort. Keep comments on topic, and do not demand answers on your schedule.
- Write in English, so that every contributor can follow the discussion.
- Respect privacy. Do not publish someone else's personal information, private messages or credentials.

## What is not acceptable

- Harassment, threats, insults or demeaning language, including about a person's origin, gender, age, disability, appearance, religion, beliefs or any other personal characteristic.
- Unwelcome sexual attention or imagery.
- Personal attacks, deliberate disruption of discussions, repeated off-topic or promotional posts, and spam.
- Publishing private information about someone without their consent.
- Encouraging or helping anyone to do any of the above.

## Reporting

If you see or experience behaviour that breaks this code, report it privately to the maintainers through GitHub: use the private reporting feature of the repository where it is offered, or contact the owners of the KingresDB organisation through their GitHub profiles. Do not post the report in a public issue or pull request. Please include where it happened, who was involved, what was said or done, and any links.

Reports are read only by the maintainers who handle them, and the reporter's identity is not shared without the reporter's consent, except where the law requires it. A person who is the subject of a report is not asked to take part in handling it.

## What happens next

The maintainers will acknowledge a report, look at what happened, and decide on a proportionate response. Responses can include a private reminder, a request to edit or remove a comment, a temporary or permanent block from a space of the project, or removal of contributions. The maintainers will tell the reporter what was decided where that is possible. Retaliation against someone who reports in good faith is itself a breach of this code.

## Scope and changes

This code applies to maintainers as well as to everyone else. Technical decisions, disputes about design and code review feedback are not breaches of this code unless they are carried out in a way that breaks it. The maintainers may update this code; changes are made through the normal change process and are visible in the history of this file.
